4: #include <memory>  // for shared_ptr, __shared_ptr_access

6: 
7: #include "ftxui/component/app.hpp"             // for App
8: #include "ftxui/component/captured_mouse.hpp"  // for ftxui
9: #include "ftxui/component/component.hpp"  // for Button, Horizontal, Renderer
10: #include "ftxui/component/component_base.hpp"  // for ComponentBase
11: #include "ftxui/dom/elements.hpp"  // for separator, gauge, text, Element, operator|, vbox, border
12: 
13: using namespace ftxui;
14: 
15: // This is a helper function to create a button with a custom style.
16: // The style is defined by a lambda function that takes an EntryState and
17: // returns an Element.
18: // We are using `center` to center the text inside the button, then `border` to
19: // add a border around the button, and finally `flex` to make the button fill
20: // the available space.
21: ButtonOption Style() {
22:   auto option = ButtonOption::Animated();
23:   option.transform = [](const EntryState& s) {
24:     auto element = text(s.label);
25:     if (s.focused) {
26:       element |= bold;
27:     }
28:     return element | center | borderEmpty | flex;
29:   };
30:   return option;
31: }
32: 
33: int main() {
34:   int value = 50;
35: 
36:   // clang-format off
37:   auto btn_dec_01 = Button("-1", [&] { value -= 1; }, Style());
38:   auto btn_inc_01 = Button("+1", [&] { value += 1; }, Style());
39:   auto btn_dec_10 = Button("-10", [&] { value -= 10; }, Style());
40:   auto btn_inc_10 = Button("+10", [&] { value += 10; }, Style());
41:   // clang-format on
42: 
43:   // The tree of components. This defines how to navigate using the keyboard.
44:   // The selected `row` is shared to get a grid layout.
45:   int row = 0;
46:   auto buttons = Container::Vertical({
47:       Container::Horizontal({btn_dec_01, btn_inc_01}, &row) | flex,
48:       Container::Horizontal({btn_dec_10, btn_inc_10}, &row) | flex,
49:   });
50: 
51:   // Modify the way to render them on screen:
52:   auto component = Renderer(buttons, [&] {
53:     return vbox({
54:                text("value = " + std::to_string(value)),
55:                separator(),
56:                buttons->Render() | flex,
57:            }) |
58:            flex | border;
59:   });
60: 
61:   auto screen = App::FitComponent();
62:   screen.Loop(component);
63:   return 0;
64: }

1: @page module-component ftxui / component
2: @tableofcontents
3: 
4: ![title-img](https://nsm09.casimages.com/img/2025/05/31//2505310207423242518595349.png)
5: 
6: The `ftxui::component` module defines the logic that produces interactive
7: components that respond to user events (keyboard, mouse, etc.).
8: 
9: The @subpage module-component-examples section provides a collection of examples.
10: 
11: A `ftxui::App` defines a main loop that renders a component.
12: 
13: A `ftxui::Component` is a shared pointer to a `ftxui::ComponentBase`. The latter defines:
14:   - `ftxui::ComponentBase::Render()`: How to render the interface.
15:   - `ftxui::ComponentBase::OnEvent()`: How to react to events.
16:   - `ftxui::ComponentBase::Add()`: Construct a parent/child relationship
17:     between two components. The tree of components is used to define how to
18:     navigate using the keyboard.
19: 
20: `ftxui::Element` are used to render a single frame.
21: 
22: `ftxui::Component` are used to render dynamic user interface, producing multiple
23: frame, and updating its state on events.
24: 
25: [Gallery](https://arthursonzogni.github.io/FTXUI/examples_2component_2gallery_8cpp-example.html) of multiple components. ([demo](https://arthursonzogni.github.io/FTXUI/examples/?file=component/gallery))
26: 
27: ![image](https://user-images.githubusercontent.com/4759106/147247330-b60beb9f-e665-48b4-81c0-4b01ee95bc66.png)
28: 
29: All predefined components are available in
30: ["ftxui/dom/component.hpp"](./component_8hpp.html)
31: 
32: \include ftxui/component/component.hpp
33: 
34: # Input {#component-input}
35: 
36: [Example](https://arthursonzogni.github.io/FTXUI/examples_2component_2input_8cpp-example.html):
37: 
38: ![image](https://user-images.githubusercontent.com/4759106/147247671-f1d6f606-1845-4e94-a4a0-d4273e9ae6bd.png)
39: 
40: Produced by: `ftxui::Input()` from "ftxui/component/component.hpp"
41: 
42: @htmlonly
43: <script id="asciicast-223719" src="https://asciinema.org/a/223719.js" async></script>
44: @endhtmlonly
45: 
46: ## Filtered input
47: 
48: One can filter out the characters received by the input component, using
49: `ftxui::CatchEvent`.
50: 
51: ```cpp
52: std::string phone_number;
53: Component input = Input(&phone_number, "phone number");
54: 
55: // Filter out non-digit characters.
56: input |= CatchEvent([&](Event event) {
57:   return event.is_character() && !std::isdigit(event.character()[0]);
58: });
59: 
60: // Filter out characters past the 10th one.
61: input |= CatchEvent([&](Event event) {
62:   return event.is_character() && phone_number.size() >= 10;
63: });
64: ```
65:

124: # Dropdown {#component-dropdown}
125: 
126: A drop-down menu is a component that, when opened, displays a list of elements
127: for the user to select from.
128: 
129: [Example](https://arthursonzogni.github.io/FTXUI/examples_2component_2dropdown_8cpp-example.html):
130: 
131: ![youtube-video-gif (3)](https://user-images.githubusercontent.com/4759106/147246982-1e821751-531c-4e1f-bc37-2fa290e143cd.gif)
132: 
133: Produced by: `ftxui::Dropdown()` from "ftxui/component/component.hpp"
134: 
135: # Slider {#component-slider}
136: 
137: Represents a slider object that consists of a range with binned intermediate
138: intervals. It can be created by `ftxui::Slider()`.
139: 
140: [Example](https://arthursonzogni.github.io/FTXUI/examples_2component_2slider_8cpp-example.html):
141: 
142: ![image](https://user-images.githubusercontent.com/4759106/147249265-7e2cad75-082c-436e-affe-44a550c480ab.png)
143: 
144: Produced by: `ftxui::Slider()` from "ftxui/component/component.hpp"
145: 
146: # Renderer {#component-renderer}
147: 
148: Produced by: `ftxui::Renderer()` from \ref ftxui/component/component.hpp. This
149: component decorate another one by using a different function to render an
150: interface.
151: 
152: Example:
153: ```cpp
154: auto inner = [...]
155: 
156: auto renderer = Renderer(inner, [&] {
157:   return inner->Render() | border
158: });
159: ```
160: 
161: `ftxui::Renderer` also supports the component decorator pattern:
162: ```cpp
163: auto component = [...]
164: component = component
165:   | Renderer([](Element e) { return e | border))
166:   | Renderer(bold)
167: ```
168: 
169: As a short hand, you can also compose a component with an element decorator:
170: ```cpp
171: auto component = [...]
172: component = component | border | bold;
173: ```
174: 
175: # CatchEvent {#component-catchevent}
176: 
177: Produced by: `ftxui::CatchEvent()` from \ref ftxui/component/component.hpp.
178: This component decorate others, catching events before the underlying component.
179: 
180: Examples:
181: ```cpp
182: auto screen = App::TerminalOutput();
183: auto renderer = Renderer([] {
184:   return text("My interface");
185: });
186: auto component = CatchEvent(renderer, [&](Event event) {
187:   if (event == Event::Character('q')) {
188:     screen.ExitLoopClosure()();
189:     return true;
190:   }
191:   return false;
192: });
193: screen.Loop(component);
194: ```
195: 
196: The `ftxui::CatchEvent` can also be used as a decorator:
197: ```cpp
198: component = component
199:   | CatchEvent(handler_1)
200:   | CatchEvent(handler_2)
201:   | CatchEvent(handler_3)
202:   ;
203: ```
204: 
205: # Collapsible {#component-collapsible}
206: 
207: Useful for visual elements whose visibility can be toggled on or off by the
208: user. Essentially, this is the combination of the `ftxui::Checkbox()` and
209: `ftxui::Maybe()` components.
210: 
211: ```cpp
212: auto collapsible = Collapsible("Show more", inner_element);
213: ```
214: 
215: # Maybe {#component-maybe}
216: 
217: Produced by: `ftxui::Maybe()` from \ref ftxui/component/component.hpp.
218: This component can be utilized to show/hide any other component via a boolean or
219: a predicate.
220: 
221: Example with a boolean:
222: ```cpp
223: bool show = true;
224: auto component = Renderer([]{ return "Hello World!"; });
225: auto maybe_component = Maybe(component, &show)
226: ```
227: 
228: Example with a predicate:
229: ```cpp
230: auto component = Renderer([]{ return "Hello World!"; });
231: auto maybe_component = Maybe(component, [&] { return time > 10; })
232: ```
233: 
234: As usual, `ftxui::Maybe` can also be used as a decorator:
235: ```cpp
236: component = component
237:   | Maybe(&a_boolean)
238:   | Maybe([&] { return time > 10; })
239:   ;
240: ```

241: 
242: # Container {#component-container}
243: 
244: ## Horizontal {#component-horizontal}
245: 
246: Produced by: `ftxui::Container::Horizontal()` from
247: "ftxui/component/component.hpp". It displays a list of components horizontally
248: and handles keyboard/mouse navigation.
249: 
250: ## Vertical {#component-vertical}
251: 
252: Produced by: `ftxui::Container::Vertical()` from
253: "ftxui/component/component.hpp". It displays a list of components vertically 
254: and handles keyboard/mouse navigation.
255: 
256: ## Tab {#component-tab}
257: 
258: Produced by: `ftxui::Container::Tab()` from
259: "ftxui/component/component.hpp". It takes a list of components and displays
260: only one of them. This is useful for implementing a tab bar.
261:

271: # ResizableSplit  {#component-resizable-split}
272: 
273: It defines a horizontal or vertical separation between two children components.
274: The position of the split is variable and controllable using the mouse. 
275: There are four possible splits:
276: - `ftxui::ResizableSplitLeft()`
277: - `ftxui::ResizableSplitRight()`
278: - `ftxui::ResizableSplitTop()`
279: - `ftxui::ResizableSplitBottom()`
280: from "ftxui/component/component.hpp"

288: @endhtmlonly
289: 
290: # Force a frame redraw. {#component-force-redraw}
291: 
292: Typically, `ftxui::App::Loop()` is responsible for drawing a new
293: frame whenever a new group of events (e.g keyboard, mouse, window resize, etc.)
294: has been processed. However, you might want to react to arbitrary events that
295: are unknown to FTXUI. To accomplish this, you must post events using
296: `ftxui::App::PostEvent` (**this is thread safe**) via a thread.
297: You will have to post the event `ftxui::Event::Custom`.
298: 
299: Example:
300: ```cpp
301: screen->PostEvent(Event::Custom);
302: ```
303: 
304: If you don't need to process a new Event, you can use:
305: ```cpp
306: screen->RequestAnimationFrame();
307: ```
308: instead.
